Oppam A Companion, Not an App

Mobile App · Prototype

A therapy app for Kerala, designed around the minutes before somebody books, the part that usually decides whether they book at all. Both sides are built: the person looking for help, and the therapist taking the sessions.

A prototype build: a real iPhone app in SwiftUI, on mock data, with nothing leaving the device.

Getting in

A name, the language you feel in, and one promise. No email, no password.

Home changes with the time of day. No badges, no counters, no streak to protect.

Finding someone

You name a feeling and meet three people with reasons attached (introductions rather than listings), then read one of them in their own words.

The bill is plain, and the last thing the booking says is that there is nothing to prepare.

The room says what it does with the session, which is nothing. Afterwards you can rebook in a tap.

Your own pages

A garden of entries, a composer whose only prompt can be switched off, and a letter you can seal for months.

Every protection explains itself, and the notification preview shows the real text a family member would see.

The companion

One face, five registers, drawn live by the app rather than by hand.

Some of it only exists in motion, so this one is a capture of it running.

The therapist’s side

Today leads with the live session and the note left last time. Nothing is timed, and the room records nothing here either.

People, not cases. A file shows a first name and only what that person chose to share.

Hours you open yourself, earnings with the split written out, and your listing exactly as somebody sees it at 2 AM.

When it goes wrong

Reassurance first, one calm retry second.

Empty is never a dead end: the companion waits in the blank space with a line and a way forward.

Dark

Warm, never cold grey. A design system is only real once the error states hold in both.
